testPolicy.text: Boston University is test optional for first-year applicants applying through fall 2028 and spring 2029, for all undergraduate schools and colleges and all scholarship programs. International students must submit TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo for English proficiency.
testPolicy.since: policy stated through fall 2028 / spring 2029 entry

cost.totalIncludes: billed: tuition 73,024 + housing 13,170 + food 7,570 + fees 1,570 = 95,334; other: books and supplies 1,000 + personal 1,455 + local transportation 630 = 3,085; total cost of attendance 98,419. Student health insurance is required under Massachusetts law unless the student has qualifying coverage (not in the total).

aidPromise.text: BU Promise: beginning in 2026-27, all domestic first-time, first-year students receive financial aid that meets 100 percent of demonstrated need without student loans. For admitted first-years starting in 2026-27 with typical assets, household income $0 to $75,000 gets full tuition plus the standard housing and dining plan covered (net cost $0); $75,001 to $100,000 pays $10,000 or less; $100,001 to $150,000 pays $15,000 or less; $150,001 to $200,000 pays $20,000 or less. BU Scholarship Assurance: first-year need-based aid is never reduced and rises by the same percentage as tuition.

facts.text: Under the BU Promise for students starting in 2026-27, families earning up to $75,000 with typical assets pay nothing for tuition, housing and dining, and those earning up to $200,000 pay at most $20,000 a year.
Early Decision fills a large share of the class: for fall 2025, BU received 6,907 ED applications and admitted 2,165, against 9,853 admits overall.
BU guarantees test-optional admission through the fall 2028 entering class, including for its merit scholarship programs.
For fall 2025, 1,075 of 9,853 admits and 500 of 3,449 enrollees were Massachusetts residents; 2,521 admits were international.
The 2026-27 cost of attendance is $98,419, of which $95,334 is billed by BU; health insurance is added if the student lacks qualifying coverage.

notes: C1: applied 30,474 men + 46,302 women (unknown-sex line blank) = 76,776, matching the residency total (8,059 in-state, 50,764 out-of-state, 15,794 international, 2,159 unknown); admitted 4,070 + 5,783 = 9,853; enrolled 1,356 + 2,093 = 3,449. CDS C12 gives the average GPA 3.86 but the percent submitting GPA was not found in the text extracted. CDS section G (posted May 2026) shows tuition 69,870, which is the 2025-26 figure (the admissions office gives 2026-27 tuition 73,024), so the admissions office figures were used for cost. No official fall 2026 numbers found: the 'Meet the Class of 2030' page has no admission statistics. ED deadline November 2 and ED2/RD January 5 come from the financial aid deadlines listed on the tuition and aid page; CDS 2025-26 lists ED II closing January 5.
